title: Perfectness under an isomorphism-induced derived equivalence
statement: Let s : X ≅ Y be a scheme isomorphism [def-pc-scheme]. Choose derived categories of module sheaves on X and all its open sites in morphism universe w₁, and on Y and all its open sites in morphism universe w₂ [def-pc-derived-category]. Let e : D(O_X) ≌ D(O_Y) have a natural isomorphism Q_X ⋙ e.functor ≅ (termwise pushforward along s.hom) ⋙ Q_Y. If E in D(O_Y) is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], then e.inverse.obj E is perfect on X. X and Y need not be affine, E need not be specified as quasi-coherent, and no relation between w₁ and w₂ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08EB, affine isomorphism transport in lem-pc-perfect-affine-finite-presentation; Tag 08CM (definition of perfection)

proof.text: Identify e.functor with the localization of exact pushforward s.hom via the supplied comparison. The module-sheaf pushforward composition and identity comparisons and uniqueness of localization identify e.inverse with localization of pushforward s.inv. The same construction applies on every pair of corresponding open sites, with the independently given derived-category choices.

source.place: Tag 08EB, affine isomorphism transport in lem-pc-perfect-affine-finite-presentation; Tag 08CM (definition of perfection)

proof.text: For x in X choose the perfect neighbourhood V of s.hom(x) and local complex K supplied by IsPerfect Y E. Put U = s.hom⁻¹(V). The isomorphism identifies the two localized sites, their structure sheaves and the restriction of the inverse derived image. The associated exact module equivalence identifies finite free modules (free modules on ULift (Fin m) are coproducts of the structure module). It preserves the splitting maps and their composite identity, zero terms and the same degree bounds. Its termwise image of K is strictly perfect on U.

source.place: Tag 08EB, affine isomorphism transport in lem-pc-perfect-affine-finite-presentation; Tag 08CM (definition of perfection)

proof.text: Apply the localized open-site functor to the model isomorphism on V and use its localization factorization and restriction compatibility. This gives the required isomorphism from restriction of e.inverse.obj E to Q of the transported strictly perfect complex on U. Membership x ∈ U is precisely s.hom(x) ∈ V. These witnesses for all x prove IsPerfect. Empty schemes and zero complexes obey the same argument.

lean.statement:
theorem scheme_iso_derived_inverse_preserves_perfect {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (s : X ≅ Y)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w₁} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w₂} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w₁} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    [∀ V : Y.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w₂} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).over V))]
    (e : schemeDerivedCategory X ≌ schemeDerivedCategory Y)
    (he : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ e.functor ≅
      (@Functor.mapHomologicalComplex ℤ
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) _ _ _ _
        (SheafOfModules.pushforward s.hom.toRingCatSheafHom)
        ⟨fun _ _ ↦ rfl⟩ (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory Y) (hE : IsPerfect Y E) :
    IsPerfect X (e.inverse.obj E)
